approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule by sampling local graph edits, including direct aromatic nitrogen relocation that preserves molecular formula. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and evaluates the first full batch allowed by short-term structural memory. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next state even after a worsening move, while a separate archive retains the best observations. Memory records a bounded, sign-balanced set of inverse local-motif changes from every selected transition. A neighbor is vetoed when both signs match one selected-transition origin. Each restriction currently expires after four completed moves, and a newer installation replaces an overlapping key.
approach.novelty: Give a restriction one additional lifetime only when that specific entry actually helped veto a neighbor during its original lifetime. This tests whether exercised structural avoidance is being forgotten too soon. The extension preserves the original transition identity and can happen only once. Earlier siblings changed which motifs receive credit, refined matching, gated credit by score or preserved overlapping origins until their original expiry. This intervention changes the lifetime of used restrictions while retaining the Parent's credit, matching and overlap rules.

hypothesis: Renew an inverse-motif restriction for exactly one additional inherited tenure when that specific live entry has actually participated in a same-transition bidirectional veto during its initial tenure, retaining its original selected-transition provenance and allowing no further renewal.

finding_summary.headline: Renewed memory replaced 62 evaluated neighbors but lowered the panel score
finding_summary.insights: This rules out a merely larger memory table or a lack of later recurrence as the explanation for the result: renewed restrictions changed both evaluated membership and selected states. Recurrence remains a weak guide to value. Of 343 renewals, 240 never participated in another qualifying veto during their observed extension, and partial matches alone accounted for 103 of those cases. More concretely, at the first DRD2 divergence in seed 1, the renewed memory excluded a neighbor that the actual Parent had scored from the identical source and selected as its winner, improving that source by 0.059783. The Child instead made a worsening move. This is direct evidence that extending an exercised restriction can remove a useful opportunity; the later endpoint loss cannot be assigned to that one veto because subsequent draws and walks diverge. The molecular assessment also finds reactive heteroatom bonds and complex sulfur cages among strongly scored structures, so this recurrence signal provides no demonstrated improvement in chemical stability or makeability. The open question is whether a task-independent signal can distinguish harmful revisits from productive reuse; actual veto participation alone did not supply that distinction in this panel.
finding_summary.results: The intended lifetime and evaluation changes both happened. All 343 used restrictions that survived to their original deadline renewed once, adding 1206 completed restriction-steps; none exceeded the eight-step limit. Renewed entries caused 65 additional vetoes in 53 batches and displaced 62 candidates from complete, reconstructed ten-member comparator batches. All 62 replacements were evaluated, seven became walk states, eight beat their source and two improved the best archive. Renewal changed at least one batch in every task/seed session, while credit selection, overlap replacement and provenance remained intact. All fifteen sessions completed their full budgets. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.513767, a paired change of -0.007992 against the required +0.002. Seeds 0 and 2 improved by 0.018110 and 0.028962, but seed 1 fell by 0.071049. Mean DRD2 score fell by 0.068863 and deco_hop by 0.008789; gains in zaleplon (+0.022797), sitagliptin (+0.013894) and median_2 (+0.000999) did not offset those losses. The renewal mechanism is confirmed; its preregistered score benefit failed.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic scaffolds coexist with reactive heteroatom bonds and sulfur cages; high scores do not establish makeability
molecular.overall_character: Read all supplied node and Parent trajectories across seeds 0, 1 and 2 and all five objectives. Each task digest covers 900 scored records, including 870 optimizer proposals; no task lacks trajectories. All optimizer proposals carry ring-closure tokens. Aromatic-token presence rates in the fixed task order are 0.9598, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.8287; these measure the presence of aromatic text, not the fraction of aromatic atoms. Every task has charged-token and stereocentre-token rates of 0.0. These are ring-rich, frequently aromatic, branched molecules with carbonyls, nitrogen heterocycles, amines, halogens and conspicuous sulfur chemistry. Some families resemble ordinary medicinal scaffolds, but the stronger observations also include large flexible decorated heteroaromatics, small strained heterocycles and densely bridged sulfur cages. The seed-specific families support moderate overall structural diversity; the 879 unique strings per task do not by themselves establish broad scaffold diversity. The same broad liabilities occur in Parent n-abcd951ab7cc. All saved optimizer molecules in both panels parse with the supplied RDKit, which establishes graph acceptance and does not establish isolation, stability, feasible conformations or a synthetic route. Quantitative molecular sizes, perceived rings and bond counts below are passive readings of the saved molecules, documented with file hashes and per-seed records in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-10-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json. All scores below were already present in the supplied trajectories. Score associations are descriptive; no excluded candidate was scored and no mechanism activation or causal efficacy is inferred.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer molecules have 21-29 heavy atoms, median 25, and 2-7 perceived rings, median 3. The strongest displayed family is a compact unsaturated O/S fused system bearing a nitrile, alkyl substituents and an aminopyridyl ketone; its best member has formula C18H17N3O2S and score 0.4619578459378901. Seed 1 retains a more conventional ethoxy/methyl/thiol-substituted indole carboxanilide as its best observation, 0.39905049777278273. Seed 2 peaks at 0.41003927643747895 with a benzofuran carboxanilide carrying N-chlorination and a chlorinated aminomethyl substituent. Those seed 1 and 2 best molecules and scores also occur in the Parent; the Parent seed 0 best is a thiophene-fused aryl ketone at 0.393567030299894. Thus the new strongest seed contains substantially different nitrile-bearing sulfur chemistry, while the other seeds retain their earlier best families. Late seed 2 proposals are more densely bridged sulfur/aryl-amide structures; the displayed final molecule scores only 0.12143963082287383. The ordinary indole and aryl-carbonyl portions are synthetically recognizable, but the higher-scoring sulfur valences and late bridges make the full structures questionable.
liabilities: Several strong structures contain nonstandard sulfur-carbon multiple bonding or hydrogen-bearing hypervalent sulfur. The late bridged systems add conformational and synthetic uncertainty.
The lower-scoring set includes N-O, N-S and hydroperoxide attachments; the seed 2 peak also contains an N-Cl bond. These liabilities are more specific than a generic objection to sulfur or halogens.
The digest reports no stereochemical annotation, despite the substituted saturated sites and bridges visible in this stream.
missing_features: Consistent retention of the compact nitrile, directly attached carbonyl and intact aminopyridyl aromatic ring is missing from the weaker local variants; rings and heteroatoms themselves are plentiful.

The stronger nitrile arrangement lacks a displayed set of chemically ordinary sulfur-free or conventional-sulfur analogues with established score retention. Such alternatives are a missing comparison, not a demonstrated objective requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Within the displayed nitrile family, changing the aminophenyl ketone ring to an aminopyridyl ring accompanies a change from 0.4229793555098886 to 0.4394278959350887; replacing the other ring sulfur with oxygen accompanies 0.4619578459378901. A particularly informative comparison is the hydroxy nitrile compound at 0.41930905650182426: its aminoethyl replacement scores 0.029336319454260972, and the analogue with the aminopyridyl ring expanded and dearomatized scores 0.021622380167913884. These observations support a compact nitrile/aryl-carbonyl/heteroaromatic arrangement in this sampled family. They do not show that unusual sulfur bonding is required, or identify an unseen reference structure.

per_task.generated_character: This stream grows large, highly decorated heteroaromatics: 30-49 heavy atoms, median 37, with 2-7 perceived rings, median 4. Every proposal contains aromatic text. The seed 2 maximum at 0.6149258916164891 has 48 heavy atoms, molecular weight about 744.421 and 18 RDKit rotatable bonds. It combines an aza-arene fused to an oxygen ring, a branched acetal-like site, an aminal, an enamine/acylurea chain, phenethyl substitution, thioethers and a sulfenyl chloride. Seed 1 instead reaches a heavily halogenated pyrazole/pyridyl amidine family; its best member at 0.5995615637559372 contains both a carbon-sulfur triple bond and a peroxide. Seed 0 retains a decorated fused N-heteroaromatic carbonyl/thiocarbonyl family, peaking at 0.5896729860129636. The corresponding Parent seed maxima are 0.6092182584436399, 0.605139548855754 and 0.6161710037174721 for seeds 2, 1 and 0 respectively. Both panels therefore contain bulky heteroaromatic decoration with difficult heteroatom chemistry; the changed scores do not indicate a transition to reliably makeable products.
liabilities: Sulfenyl chlorides or fluorides, sulfenate/peroxide attachments, N-halogenation and a carbon-sulfur triple bond occur in strongly scored families.
The strongest seed 2 molecule is large and highly flexible; the seed 1 peak is heavy through extensive halogenation. Both add synthetic complexity beyond the recognizable heteroaromatic core.
Aminal/acetal-like centers and unsaturated N-rich connections have unspecified configurations; their stability and stereochemical form are not established by these scores.
missing_features: Chemically stable, compact redecoration around the observed aromatic/polar arrangement is underrepresented relative to the long branched side chains. The methoxy replacement provides a concrete score-compatible simplification of one labile attachment.
Intact aromatic presentation is not consistently preserved in the poorer ring-edited neighbours. The observed scores do not identify a particular unseen scaffold or decoration as the answer.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623. Early ring-distorted and ring-opened variants lie around the displayed 0.526081691583997-0.530944810356575, while later substituted heteroaromatic and amidine/acylurea families approach the higher scores. Within the late seed 2 family, the additional amino group at the aryl-linked aminal accompanies 0.6149258916164891 versus 0.5998381003777657 without it. Replacing the O-S-C substituent with O-O-C leaves the latter score exactly unchanged, and replacing it with methoxy yields 0.6017009213323884. Expanding and dearomatizing the terminal phenyl ring gives 0.5501836618552434. The observed arrangement of aromatic and polar groups matters, but the score often tolerates chemically consequential changes in peripheral heteroatom bonds.

per_task.generated_character: All optimizer proposals contain rings, aromatic text and halogens. They span 31-43 heavy atoms, median 37, with 2-10 perceived rings, median 4. The strongest seed 0 family has a tertiary aliphatic amine between hydrophobic arylalkyl groups and a small S/N-ring thioamide; the best member at 0.934280163121624 has 33 heavy atoms, two aromatic rings and two four-membered rings, including a benzofused ether. The seed 2 maximum 0.9527396692852879 has 32 heavy atoms and an aminoethyl connection between an N/S-rich ring framework and a fluorinated aryl/sulfur ring system. Seed 1 instead forms a densely connected conjugated polycycle, peaking at 0.5748505647663341. Parent best scores for seeds 0, 1 and 2 are 0.8856242185485628, 0.868020189804352 and 0.9148143511682032; both panels retain halogenated aromatic/basic-nitrogen frameworks and unusual sulfur chemistry. The stronger node molecules therefore change the detailed ring/linker presentation without demonstrating better synthetic plausibility.
liabilities: Hydrogen-bearing hypervalent sulfur, sulfur multiple bonds, small strained S/N or fused ether rings, and N-S attachments complicate the strongest structures.

Every one of the 870 optimizer molecules has an unassigned RDKit potential tetrahedral center. Dense polycycles and substituted amines are consequently represented without a defined stereochemical product.
All submitted structures are formally neutral even when they contain potentially basic amines. Neutral SMILES do not establish absence of ionization or the microstate used by the scoring procedure.
missing_features: Reliable access to ordinary saturated amine-ring and linker geometries that preserve the favorable aryl separation is missing from the stronger but structurally unusual families. Basic nitrogen and aromatic rings are already present.
Defined configurations and explicit chemical microstates are absent from the submitted representation. The trajectories do not measure whether adding those representations would change the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bulky acid/amide/sulfonamide starting family scores 0.01904115112334333, with a displayed early analogue at 0.007468397818197266. The stronger late molecules expose non-acylated aliphatic nitrogen centers and differently spaced hydrophobic aryl groups. A basic center alone is insufficient: the initial N-methylpiperidine/hydroxamate molecule scores only 0.0003786988088202195. In a close late pair, replacing a carbon in the aminoethyl linker with sulfur accompanies a fall from 0.9228850624978101 to 0.25489749232435305; expanding and dearomatizing the pyridyl ring of the same high-scoring framework yields 0.22677113885646957. The sampled evidence points to the combined amine, linker and aromatic arrangement. It does not isolate a binding interaction or prove that the strained sulfur rings are beneficial.

per_task.generated_character: The output contains aryl/aza-aryl rings attached to N-rich cyclic carbonyl frameworks, often with N-O bridges. Optimizer molecules have 27-43 heavy atoms, median 35, and 3-8 perceived rings, median 4. The seed 0 maximum 0.21196904390980506 is a 31-heavy-atom aza-arene/tolyl lactam with a densely bridged N-O framework. RDKit perceives seven rings in that graph; this overlapping ring description is not seven independently accessible synthetic building blocks. Seed 2 reaches a 38-heavy-atom polycyclic aminoether/lactam bearing N-O and N-N bonds at 0.20728376879781038. Seed 1 favors an aryl thioester/cyclic-urea family containing an O-Br bond, with best score 0.18849200938442048. Parent seed 0 has the identical best molecule and score, while Parent seeds 1 and 2 peak at 0.19092251395438758 and 0.20185639717998205. Ordinary aryl and carbonyl chemistry remains recognizable across both panels, but it is embedded in increasingly complicated bridges or reactive peripheral groups.
liabilities: Overlapping large rings, N-O bridges and N-N-containing connections make conformation, stereochemistry and synthesis uncertain even when the elemental composition looks conventional.

The seed 1 stream includes O-Br bonds, S-Br connections and heavily brominated sulfur centers. These are concrete reactive-bond concerns, and do not establish that all thioesters or N-O groups are intrinsically unacceptable.
RDKit finds unassigned potential tetrahedral centers in 759 of 870 optimizer molecules; the supplied SMILES do not define the configurations of the bridged products.
missing_features: The stronger aryl/lactam arrangement lacks a demonstrated family of simpler, conformationally credible constrained analogues. Additional bridges and local alkyl changes do not establish the needed broader structural match.
Broader coherent arrangements of the existing aromatic and carbonyl groups are missing from the displayed high-score cluster; neither aromaticity nor carbonyl presence itself is scarce.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The displayed ring-opened aryl-pyrrole carbonyl/urea chains score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515, below the more constrained aryl/lactam arrangements. Within the seed 0 bridged family, an alkyl-substituent change accompanies 0.2087472610464947 versus 0.21196904390980506, and a phenolic analogue scores 0.20867364616432552. These are modest variations within a limited family. The later brominated sulfur compounds still contain aromatic rings and carbonyls but reach displayed low scores such as 0.13085321445798428. The signal supports particular aryl/carbonyl relationships and constrained connectivity, not simply more rings, halogens or heteroatoms. The full best score remains 0.21196904390980506, so no high-quality match to an unseen desired structure can be inferred.

per_task.generated_character: These are compact in atom count but highly intricate sulfur-rich cages: 26-34 heavy atoms, median 30, and 3-9 perceived rings, median 6. The aromatic-token presence rate is 0.8287, yet the best seed 0 and seed 2 molecules have no RDKit aromatic rings. The seed 0 maximum 0.48118636011729826 has 30 heavy atoms, eight sulfur atoms and six perceived rings, including carbonyl and acyl-fluoride functionality. It is identical to the Parent best for that seed. Seed 1 peaks at 0.5362860575674161 with 31 heavy atoms, four sulfur atoms, fluorinated substituents and an imide-like carbonyl core embedded in seven rings; the corresponding Parent maximum is 0.5903526424693334 in another sulfur cage. The node seed 2 best 0.5442045058478946 has 30 heavy atoms, five sulfur atoms, eight perceived rings, an explicit S#S bond and an N-F bond, compared with a Parent cage maximum of 0.4484554129767839. The high scores therefore remain attached to chemically exceptional cage structures, with particularly poor apparent makeability despite successful graph parsing.
liabilities: Neutral sulfur-sulfur triple bonds, hydrogen-bearing hypervalent sulfur and multiply bonded sulfur bridges dominate the unusual chemistry. Passive counting finds sulfur triple bonds in 111 of 870 node proposals, versus 91 of 870 Parent proposals.

The strongest examples also contain N-F bonds, an acyl fluoride or sulfur-linked fluorohydrin-like sites, together with densely fused small rings. These combinations make stability and practical synthesis especially doubtful.

The best seed 0, 1 and 2 graphs have respectively nine, nine and five unassigned RDKit potential tetrahedral centers. Ring closure in a valid graph does not establish a physically attainable stereochemical cage.
missing_features: A chemically credible realization of the polar carbonyl/fluorinated ring arrangement is missing from the displayed strongest molecules. Ordinary sulfur connectivity with retained score has not been demonstrated for these cages.
Defined and geometrically feasible cage configurations are missing. The observed evidence does not support prescribing extra aromatic rings or a specific amine as an unseen objective requirement.

Much stronger structures still share carbonyls, nitrogen, fluorine and sulfur, showing that their arrangement and the whole graph matter more than the mere presence of those features. A displayed seed 2 pair differing by S-S versus S#S bonding ties exactly at 0.4977611135431298. Expanding a small sulfur ring in a related cage accompanies 0.5442045058478946 versus 0.4823284954539163. The displayed final sulfur-deleted variant falls to 0.11163119096253812. These sharp local changes and exact ties do not reveal a conventional pharmacophore or establish chemically sensible sulfur valence as something the objective rewards.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A displayed structure at 0.5442045058478946 contains an explicit sulfur-sulfur triple bond. A related single-bond/triple-bond pair ties at 0.4977611135431298. One complete proposal stream contains 111 sulfur-triple-bond molecules out of 870, and both the node and Parent also contain hydrogen-bearing hypervalent sulfur cages. Graph acceptance and a strong observed score therefore coexist with sulfur chemistry of doubtful makeability.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably realize its strongly scored ring frameworks with ordinary sulfur connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose chemically ordinary sulfur valence and connectivity alternatives around the observed ring frameworks, with explicit molecular validity beyond parsing. Use ordinary task-local feedback to determine score retention; the existing ties supply no reward justification for the exceptional bond orders, and no universal score benefit from restricting sulfur is established.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The same branched heteroaromatic family scores 0.5998381003777657 with either an O-S-C attachment or an O-O-C attachment, while its methoxy replacement scores 0.6017009213323884. Strong or persistent families also contain sulfenyl halides, N-halogen bonds and O-Br bonds. Those attachments are not necessary for the one demonstrated methoxy-compatible arrangement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently separate useful scaffold features from reactive peripheral heteroatom bonds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate matched, chemically stable replacements for peroxide, sulfenyl-halide and heteroatom-halogen connections while preserving the surrounding scaffold. Measure each replacement through the existing feedback rather than treating a peripheral score tie as evidence that the underlying bonds are chemically equivalent.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A hydroxy nitrile structure at 0.41930905650182426 falls to 0.029336319454260972 when its nitrile is replaced by an aminoethyl group. Another close family falls from 0.9228850624978101 to 0.25489749232435305 when a carbon in its aminoethyl linker becomes sulfur. Ring expansion and loss of aromaticity also accompany lower scores in several displayed comparisons. Rings and heteroatoms remain abundant on both sides of these contrasts.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful polar-group and aromatic arrangements are not consistently preserved during local chemical variation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide coherent matched changes in linker length, attachment position, ring size and polar-group placement that preserve other established molecular features. Let the observed score response determine which arrangements to retain; these examples support control of relative placement without naming or identifying an objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One maximum is a 48-heavy-atom structure with 18 rotatable bonds, while another is a 30-heavy-atom cage with eight perceived rings. A separate aryl/lactam maximum has seven overlapping perceived rings and an N-O bridge. The displayed high-score groups remain concentrated in related decorated families even though every task contains 879 unique molecular strings. Ordinary rings are plentiful, but balanced flexibility and manageable ring construction are not consistently demonstrated.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks a consistent path to simpler, feasible analogues of its strongest molecular arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Explore scaffold-preserving simplifications and coherent alternative ring connections that retain useful aromatic and polar relationships while reducing unnecessary branches or overlapping closures. Judge those variants by their actual feedback and chemical feasibility; the observed range supplies no single preferred atom count or ring count.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-token and charged-token rates of 0.0. The scored molecules include substituted saturated amines, bridged N/O systems and fluorinated sulfur cages; one full stream has an unassigned potential tetrahedral center in every one of its 870 optimizer molecules. Several best cage graphs have many unassigned centers. Neutral representations also coexist with potentially ionizable amine groups.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves the stereochemical and ionization identities of chemically complex products unresolved.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent feasible configurations and chemically coherent protonation states explicitly when varying stereogenic or ionizable structures. Preserve the distinction between a defined molecular product and a new score-bearing identity: these trajectories establish the representation gap, but do not establish an objective benefit from state enumeration.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

activation_observables.measurement: For every installed version reconstruct initial expiry, qualifying first-use event, overlap replacement, release, renewal and final expiry. Report installed entries, entries used during their initial window, used entries surviving to expiry, renewed entries and their realized extra completed steps, with termination-censored lifetimes separate. Parent references are 1711 installed entries, 380 distinct used entries, 1431 expirations and 344 used expirations. Require eligible surviving entries to receive exactly one extra inherited tenure, unused entries to expire at their original deadline, and every version to disappear no later than twice the inherited tenure unless the task ends first. finding_summary.headline: Renewed memory replaced 62 evaluated neighbors but lowered the panel score
finding_summary.insights: This rules out a merely larger memory table or a lack of later recurrence as the explanation for the result: renewed restrictions changed both evaluated membership and selected states. Recurrence remains a weak guide to value. Of 343 renewals, 240 never participated in another qualifying veto during their observed extension, and partial matches alone accounted for 103 of those cases. More concretely, at the first DRD2 divergence in seed 1, the renewed memory excluded a neighbor that the actual Parent had scored from the identical source and selected as its winner, improving that source by 0.059783. The molecular assessment also finds reactive heteroatom bonds and complex sulfur cages among strongly scored structures, so this recurrence signal provides no demonstrated improvement in chemical stability or makeability. The open question is whether a task-independent signal can distinguish harmful revisits from productive reuse; actual veto participation alone did not supply that distinction in this panel.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich aromatic scaffolds coexist with reactive heteroatom bonds and sulfur cages; high scores do not establish makeability
molecular_assessment.overall_character: Read all supplied node and Parent trajectories across seeds 0, 1 and 2 and all five objectives. Each task digest covers 900 scored records, including 870 optimizer proposals; no task lacks trajectories. All optimizer proposals carry ring-closure tokens. Aromatic-token presence rates in the fixed task order are 0.9598, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.8287; these measure the presence of aromatic text, not the fraction of aromatic atoms. Every task has charged-token and stereocentre-token rates of 0.0. These are ring-rich, frequently aromatic, branched molecules with carbonyls, nitrogen heterocycles, amines, halogens and conspicuous sulfur chemistry. Some families resemble ordinary medicinal scaffolds, but the stronger observations also include large flexible decorated heteroaromatics, small strained heterocycles and densely bridged sulfur cages. The seed-specific families support moderate overall structural diversity; the 879 unique strings per task do not by themselves establish broad scaffold diversity. The same broad liabilities occur in Parent n-abcd951ab7cc. All saved optimizer molecules in both panels parse with the supplied RDKit, which establishes graph acceptance and does not establish isolation, stability, feasible conformations or a synthetic route. Quantitative molecular sizes, perceived rings and bond counts below are passive readings of the saved molecules, documented with file hashes and per-seed records in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-10-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json. All scores below were already present in the supplied trajectories. Score associations are descriptive; no excluded candidate was scored and no mechanism activation or causal efficacy is inferred.

A restriction must participate in an actual veto before its original deadline and remain live until that deadline. No renewal occurs for isolated partial matches, overwritten or released versions, unused versions, or termination-censored versions. The policy uses no score threshold or objective identity.

approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule by sampling local graph edits, including direct aromatic nitrogen relocation that preserves molecular formula. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and evaluates the first full batch allowed by short-term structural memory. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next state even after a worsening move, while a separate archive retains the best observations. Memory records a bounded, sign-balanced set of inverse local-motif changes from every selected transition. A neighbor is vetoed when both signs match one selected-transition origin. Each restriction currently expires after four completed moves, and a newer installation replaces an overlapping key.
approach.novelty: Give a restriction one additional lifetime only when that specific entry actually helped veto a neighbor during its original lifetime. This tests whether exercised structural avoidance is being forgotten too soon. The extension preserves the original transition identity and can happen only once. Earlier siblings changed which motifs receive credit, refined matching, gated credit by score or preserved overlapping origins until their original expiry. This intervention changes the lifetime of used restrictions while retaining the Parent's credit, matching and overlap rules.

research_intent.mechanism: Renew an inverse-motif restriction for exactly one additional inherited tenure when that specific live entry has actually participated in a same-transition bidirectional veto during its initial tenure, retaining its original selected-transition provenance and allowing no further renewal.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-abcd951ab7cc completes its supplied panel with macro mean 0.5217591163770486 and standard deviation 0.006329100643035156. Its actual summary.json and run.log files all report successful completion. Its fixed expiry rule makes no distinction between an unused restriction and one repeatedly exercised by the local proposal stream. A read-only reconstruction of all fifteen saved task logs finds 435 installations containing 1711 entries, 46 overlap replacements, 4545 valid-novel tests and 195 actual vetoes. Of 1431 expired entries, 344 had participated in an actual same-transition bidirectional veto during their original lifetime; 380 distinct entries participated overall. Filtering the passive renewed table back to each entry's original expiry reproduces every one of the 4545 logged Parent blocking sets exactly. On the same recorded selected histories and candidate draws, one additional original tenure for the used entries renews 344 records and adds 54 vetoes across 48 batches, involving 96 renewed entries; the maximum passive live table contains 30 entries. These are conditional opportunity measurements, not a generated or scored alternative walk. The 54 historically evaluated neighbors include six source improvements, two ties, 46 losses, six selected states and three archive gains, so recurring inverse-motif matches are not known to be unproductive. The overlap-preservation sibling n-52759efc37a6 changed only one evaluated batch and missed its score target. The score-gated and complete-signature siblings n-a240f72e3717 and n-7c411fdf5a88 also activated but lost panel score. Together these findings leave demand-dependent expiry unresolved rather than establishing that more or fewer vetoes alone are beneficial.
research_intent.revisit_rationale: The broad expiring inverse-memory cluster includes Knowledge-only interventions whose credit, matching and overlap mechanisms activated without their registered score benefit. This is a different causal question within that family: all those memory siblings retained the original fixed lifetime, and independent overlapping provenance only prevented overwrite until the original deadline. The new explanation being tested is that actual proposal-stream recurrence supplies evidence for retaining a particular exercised restriction beyond that deadline, while keeping every installation and the bidirectional predicate intact. The actual Parent provides 344 used-but-expiring versions and a conditional 54 later veto opportunities, compared with the overlap child's one changed batch. Neither those opportunities nor the failed relaxations prove longer protection useful; they justify a separate bounded lifetime intervention with real allocation and score falsifiers. The Parent mechanism stack is unchanged, and no failed sibling intervention is added.
